task.goal: Write the life this cycle's record produced. Lead with a named interviewed person or a Packet-named place. The feed or tracker line is the weather, never the lede.
task.approach: Long-view approach (Simon Leary): third-person essayist. Treat supplied sports facts as present structure, not as proof of history or collective memory. A metaphor about continuity, load, or change may interpret the Packet but may not add a person, place, institution, event, season, statistic, cause, organizational intention, or citywide belief. Do not write a game recap, Hal elegy, P Slayer fan heat, or Anthony board memo.

creativeBrief.claim: A role change inside a sustained team record can support a structural interpretation; it does not establish franchise history, organizational intent, or citywide meaning.
missing: why the role change was made
creativeBrief.sceneRule: No witnessed room or scene is supplied. Structure and continuity may appear only as clearly interpretive metaphor grounded in the approved present facts.

plan.focus: The structural interpretation of a role change inside a sustained 2-0 record—what it means for continuity when the load-bearing pieces shift.
plan.closeQuestion: When the record stays perfect but the structure underneath shifts, what does that say about the nature of continuity itself?

sources.name: Adash Stanley
sources.quote: When the role changes, the record doesn't care who's carrying it. It just sits there at 2-0 and asks the next guy to keep it honest. For me, that means showing up the same way I always have — steady, ready, not making it about me. The continuity is in the work, not the title.

sources.name: Austin Reaves
sources.quote: Look, 2-0 feels good, don't get me wrong. But I've been around long enough to know a record doesn't hold the building up. It's the guys inside it. We're still figuring out who we are out there — roles, rotations, all that. The structure shifting? That's just part of the game. You don't carry the weight by pretending everything's locked in. You carry it by showing up, doing your job, and trusting the guys next to you. That's what I'm doing. That's all I can do.

excludedLeads.text: The role change might be tied to a player's condition or a strategic adjustment, but that's not in the packet.
There may be a deeper story about how the team is handling the early-season pressure, but I have no evidence for it.
The community might be reacting to the role change, but I have no source for that.

limits.rule: The Packet is what you know, not the fence around what you may write. The approved facts and the ledger are canon: never contradict them, and never import real-world Oakland (its people, businesses, landmarks, troubles). Everything else — the scene, the street, the weather in the room, unnamed people and what they say, new in-world places and businesses, what the city is talking about — is yours to invent; that colour is the job, and it never rewrites a canon fact. A named ledger citizen speaks only in their approved quote or their own page line. Do not brief the record. Open on a person or place living the condition.
